question: How do Morgan Stanley and Merrill differ in how they segment clients by wealth tier?

claims.text: Asset thresholds - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) describes Wealth Management clients only in general terms, as individual investors "including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions." No numeric asset or investable-asset tiers appear in the evidence.

Asset thresholds - Merrill: The BAC 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business is staffed by financial advisors "focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets." It says Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, targets high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. The 10-K gives no dollar figure for that upper tier.

Asset thresholds - Merrill: In footnotes to the 1Q26 deck (published 2026-04-15), the 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) and the 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-14), Bank of America defines Merrill primary households as "$250K+ in investable assets." It defines Private Bank core relationships as "$3MM+ in total balances."

Asset thresholds - Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets. He said the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management. The 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) reports about 5.4K net new $500K+ households in Merrill and about 430 net new $3MM+ relationships in the Private Bank.

Channels - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that Wealth Management "supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace." The 2Q26 supplement (published 2026-07-15) reports advisor-led client assets of $6,273 billion and self-directed client assets of $1,811 billion at June 30, 2026. It also reports stock plan unvested public assets of $658 billion for the workplace channel. Channel is the organizing line in the evidence, not wealth tier.

Channels - Merrill: The BAC 10-Q for 2Q26 (published 2026-07-31) says GWIM "consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank." The 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) shows client balances at period end of $4,240,601 million for Merrill Wealth Management and $816,186 million for Bank of America Private Bank. The 2025 10-K places Private Wealth Management inside Merrill Wealth Management and pairs it with the Private Bank for high net worth and ultra high net worth clients.

Service model - Morgan Stanley: Per the 4Q25 supplement (published 2026-01-15), advisor-led client assets are "client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned." Self-directed client assets are "active accounts which are not advisor-led," and active means at least $25 in assets. The workplace channel "includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees." On the 1Q25 call (April 2025) the CFO said about $300 billion had migrated into advisor-led accounts from workplace since the channel was expanded in 2020. Management describes this as a funnel of relationships feeding the advisor-led channel.

Service model - Merrill: The BAC 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as "a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors," offering investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products. It describes the Private Bank and Private Wealth Management offering as comprehensive wealth management solutions with customized wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking services, including specialty asset management. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with Bank of America.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's self-directed channel counts only "active accounts" with at least $25 in assets (4Q25 supplement, published 2026-01-15). Its Core Client Relationships metric counts Advisor-Led Households, Self-Directed Households and Workplace Participants (strategic update deck, published 2026-01-15).
adjacent.differs_because: These are definitions of account activity and relationship counts by channel. They are not wealth-tier thresholds.

adjacent.text: A trade-press item (published 2026-10-02) refers to Merrill Edge online accounts in a cash-sweep settlement. No evidence chunk describes Merrill Edge as a defined client tier or service model.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative. It mentions Merrill Edge in a litigation context and does not describe how clients are segmented.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley - asset thresholds: not found in the evidence provided. No numeric asset or investable-asset thresholds for any wealth tier appear, and the evidence names no tiered service model by wealth level.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management investor presentations, Form ADV Part 2A, or advisor-led account minimums disclosures

gaps.what: Merrill - Merrill Edge: not found in the evidence provided. No disclosure of Merrill Edge's client threshold or service model appears. The $250K, $500K and $3MM markers come from Bank of America GWIM disclosures.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America Consumer Banking segment disclosures or the Merrill Edge product pages

gaps.what: Merrill - upper-tier threshold: the evidence gives $3MM+ only as a Private Bank relationship definition. It gives no dollar threshold for Private Wealth Management within Merrill, and no tier-by-tier service model beyond the 10-K descriptions.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America/Merrill Private Wealth Management marketing materials or Form ADV Part 2A
